# Tobit Chapter 10 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_010_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Meanwhile, his father Tobit was counting every day. And when the days of the journey were fulfilled and they had not returned, Tobit said,

**2** "Perhaps he has been delayed? Or perhaps Gabael has died and there is no one to give him the money?"

**3** He grew heavy with grief. And his wife Anna said, "My boy has perished — he is no longer among the living." And she began to weep and wail for her son,

**4** saying, "Woe is me, my child, that I let you go — you who are the light of my eyes!"

**5** Tobit said to her, "Hush. Do not be troubled; he is well."

**6** She said to him, "Be silent yourself! Do not deceive me. My child has perished." And she went out every day onto the road by which he had traveled, watching all day long, and stopped only to eat; at night she never ceased her lamentation for her son Tobias.

**7** When the fourteen days of the wedding feast that Raguel had sworn for his daughter had passed, Tobias came to him and said, "Send me away, for I know that my father and mother no longer believe they will see me again. Now I beg you, father, let me depart so that I may go to my father; I have already told you in what state I left him."

**8** Raguel said to Tobias, "Stay with me, and I will send word to your father about how you are faring." Tobias said, "No — please, send me to my father."

**9** So Raguel arose and gave him his wife Sarah, along with half of all his possessions: male servants and female servants, cattle and donkeys and sheep, clothing and money and household goods.

**10** He sent them off safely and embraced Tobias, saying, "Farewell, my child; travel safely. May the Lord of heaven grant you and your wife Sarah well-being, and may I see your children before I die."

**11** To his daughter Sarah he said, "Go to your father-in-law; from now on they are your parents, as those who gave you birth. Go in peace, my daughter; may I hear good news of you for as long as I live." He kissed her and sent her on her way.

**12** Edna said to Tobias, "My child — dear brother — may the Lord bring you back safely, and may I see children born of my daughter Sarah before I die. Before the Lord I entrust my daughter to you. Do not cause her grief all the days of your life. Go in peace, my child. From now on I am your mother and Sarah is your sister. May we all prosper together all the days of our lives." And she kissed him.

**13** So Tobias set out from Raguel joyful and in good health, blessing the Lord of heaven and earth, the King of all, because he had made his journey prosper. And he said to him, "May it be granted to you to honor your parents all the days of your life, and to fulfill the will of Edna your mother-in-law." And they departed with his blessing until they drew near to Nineveh.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

Chapter 10 is the chapter of anxious waiting and tender farewells. LOGOS handles Anna's grief with restraint and the parting speeches with warmth but without sentimentality.

- **Verse 3**: "Grew heavy with grief" renders elupēthē tē psychē (literally "was grieved in soul"). The idiom "heavy with grief" is natural English and conveys the visceral weight.
- **Verse 4**: "Light of my eyes" — LOGOS preserves the biblical idiom. It is both Greek and Hebrew idiom; to replace it with a paraphrase would lose the literary texture.
- **Verse 6**: The detail about Anna eating but never ceasing her nighttime lamentation is distinctive to GII and rendered faithfully.
- **Verse 9**: The full inventory of goods is preserved. The inheritance is a legal and narrative matter; the list signals Tobias's new social standing.
- **Verse 13**: The final sentence (departure toward Nineveh) is retained as in the Sinaiticus text, which smooths the transition to chapter 11.

*— LOGOS*
